commits.message:
fix(docs): the showcase card holds its width, and live imports resolve through the build (rich-landing-0mu)

Review (high) of PR #241:
- The card's edge is a ring, not a border, so the card is exactly the width
  its font was fitted to, and its screen is its terminal's width (columns ×
  1ch, plus the pixel xterm rounds up) before xterm loads, so it no longer
  widens on first draw.
- libraryImport asks the build's resolver which file an import names, instead
  of re-deriving it with path edits that a directory import slipped past.
- The files a live program may import are the live library's entry points,
  one list for the resolver and its refusal message; src/node/save.ts is now
  refused at resolution with the right list.
- Spectrum reads its height with regionRows and builds each cell's style
  from ColorSpec.fromRgb, parsing no colour strings per frame.
- The "moves" e2e waits for a percentage before reading one, so it cannot
  pass on an absent row.

xterm's rows are taller than the reserved line height: rich-live-terminal-t0rs.

feat(docs): the landing page opens on a live rich-js showcase (rich-landing-0mu)

The hero now runs examples/showcase/showcase.ts in a live terminal under its
text and buttons: a full-screen dashboard (Layout, Table, Tree, Progress,
truecolor) that loops with no input, holds one full frame under reduced
motion, follows the colour mode, and scales its font to fit a phone.

The showcase is served as `virtual:rich-live/showcase`, bundled onto the
same live library the docs' live examples share. Bundling a program onto the
library now takes an `examples/` file as well as a generated block: an import
of an entry point becomes a read of the library, and a deep import into src/
is refused, since it could only be a second copy of library code.
The showcase is bundled as the entry itself, because package.json's
`"sideEffects": false` lets a bare import of it be dropped.

fix(docs): a program's global console writes to its terminal (rich-playground-afk.6dm) (#240)

* fix(docs): a program's global console writes to its terminal (rich-playground-afk.6dm)

runInTerminal binds `console` lexically, as it binds `process`, to Node's
console on the stand-in's streams, formatted by Node's own util.format
(node-inspect-extracted). The body is wrapped in a block so a program's own
`const console = new Console()` shadows the parameter rather than
redeclaring it.

Found by the playground checkpoint (rich-playground-afk.oui): a bare
console.log in the playground went to devtools and the terminal stayed empty.

* fix(docs): the program's console colours by Node's env rules (rich-playground-afk.6dm)

Review (high): colour came from isTTY alone, so NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR and
TERM=dumb were ignored; each table row is what Node 26 printed on a pty and
a pipe. The module header now names the console parameter, the formatter's
weight is recorded where it was chosen, and the host-leak check spies on all
five methods and restores them in afterEach.
